warnings.text: From 2053 (age 65) your savings and investments and pension can’t cover your spending. The gap is shown as an unfunded shortfall.
You haven’t chosen what to do with your leftover money, so the projection doesn’t save any of it (it’s treated as spent).

suggestions.title: Higher-rate pension relief
suggestions.text: You pay 40% tax on your top slice of pay, so each £1 into your pension costs you only about 60p. Salary sacrifice also saves National Insurance.
howTo: Ask payroll or HR to raise your contribution from 5% to 8%: about £213 a month going in, costing you about £128 after tax relief.
If they offer salary sacrifice, ask about it: it saves National Insurance as well as tax.
Check your next payslip: about £213 more a month should be going in.

commitment.what: Raise your pension contribution from 5% to 8%

suggestions.title: Check for employer matching
suggestions.text: Your employer adds 3%. Many employers add more if you pay more — if yours does, that’s usually the best return available.

suggestions.title: Use your ISA allowance
suggestions.text: You have about £20,000 of this year’s £20,000 ISA allowance left. Growth and interest in an ISA are tax-free. For money you won’t need for at least five years, a stocks & shares ISA has historically beaten cash, but can fall in value.
howTo: Set up £1,570 a month into a stocks & shares ISA (or a cash ISA for money you’ll need within five years). Open one, or top up one you already have.
You have about £20,000 of this year’s allowance left, and 163 days until it resets on 5 April 2027.
Set the payment for payday so it happens without thinking about it.

commitment.what: Pay £1,570 a month into an ISA
